data.narrative: The Module 08 retrospective records scoped feature coverage, five quality dimensions, available process metrics, and honest time-measurement limits. Two mocked suites (22 tests) passed, the Nest build and diff check exited 0, and PostgreSQL reachability returned False; database-backed integration and live HTTP checks remain NOT EXECUTED. The report identifies the fixed-seed integration assumption, missing verified CI workflow, invitation-email privacy policy, and process-local feed boundary as remaining release work.

dimension_scores.observation: The production-grade task constraints and evidence boundaries were kept explicit.
dimension_scores.evidence: The retrospective ties the scoped API, authorization, database, test, and release requirements to their artifacts.

dimension_scores.observation: The review covered feature behavior, test isolation, API documentation, CI readiness, privacy, and deployment limits.
dimension_scores.evidence: The Module 08 artifacts include endpoint/readiness checks, the pre-seeded identity finding, and process-local SSE limitations.

dimension_scores.observation: Scoped reviews and combined mocked verification produced focused feedback without claiming unmeasured time savings.
dimension_scores.evidence: The two mocked suites ran together with 22 passing tests; historical prompt/iteration counts and wall-clock project time are explicitly marked not recorded.

dimension_scores.observation: Claims distinguish source and mocked evidence from live database, HTTP, CI, and multi-instance behavior.
dimension_scores.evidence: The PostgreSQL probe returned False, so live database and HTTP verification remain NOT EXECUTED; shared pub/sub is not claimed verified.

dimension_scores.observation: The reflection gives a useful handoff with reproducible proof, named residual risks, and concrete release gates.
dimension_scores.evidence: It includes the exact test/build/diff/database outputs, decision callback, comprehension themes, and mini-practical risk/mitigation.

strengths: Separates mocked verification from database-backed and live HTTP evidence.
Identifies clean-CI fixture assumptions and process-local event-delivery limits.
Connects production readiness to concrete CI, database, privacy, and rollout work.
data.recommendation: Before production sign-off, provision and migrate only url_shortener_test, make integration tests create and clean their own identities and records, execute the authenticated HTTP journey in CI, define audit-email retention, and verify shared pub/sub if the service is multi-instance.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: The reflection states that mocks and compilation do not establish live persistence, HTTP middleware behavior, or multi-instance delivery.
The retrospective treats clean database setup, migrations, integration tests, CI execution, privacy policy, and rollback as release gates.
The reflection identifies fixed pre-seeded identities as a clean-CI risk and recommends test-owned setup, generated IDs, and failure-tolerant cleanup.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the passing mocked test output and failed PostgreSQL reachability probe to distinguish verified behavior from pending integration evidence.
Mapped each remaining production claim to the database, HTTP, CI, privacy, or shared-delivery check needed to support it.

public_evidence.student_action: Recorded the final module verification and production-readiness boundaries.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Combined the team activity-feed and collaboration contract suites with a Nest build and repository diff check.
public_evidence.proof: Jest reported 2 suites and 22 tests passed; Nest build exited 0; git diff --check exited 0; PostgreSQL reachability returned False, leaving live DB/HTTP checks NOT EXECUTED.
public_evidence.ability: Evaluates release evidence and distinguishes local checks from production verification.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows clear reporting of verified behavior, environment limits, and remaining release gates.
